question: Does sequential outward projection supply a clear reusable contour/line deformation capability, and is fractional strength visibly useful independent of source styling?
source_limitation: Survey flatten_0.8 changes x interpolation only; its subtle result cannot establish a symmetric strength range.
study: Independently authored JAVA2D study; fixed points and ordered discs, same geometry at strength0,0.45,1. Show a sampled closed contour and an open parallel-line family using identical projection arithmetic. A separate overlapping-disc case reverses influence order.
private_semantics: For each point, visit supplied discs in order. If distance d<radius, move toward the radial boundary by strength*(radius-d) along the normalized point-minus-center direction. Exact center uses positiveX. Zero strength and points outside/on boundary remain unchanged. This is a one-pass deformation, not collision resolution; later discs may undo earlier exclusion.
retain_if: Both consumers visibly exhibit understandable local deformation; fractional strength is distinguishable from identity and full projection without needing owner-disc-specific recovery or appearance constants.
reject_or_revise_if: Useful output requires the complete source-specific owner ray/envelope machinery, or the controls cannot be explained without promising nonoverlap or polygon containment.
bounds: Private finite canvas-scale inputs only; 720x480, at most four discs and4000 supplied points; three strength views plus one order comparison. No public numeric bounds/defaults frozen.
acceptance: Root reads prototype and inspects actual images. No production code, shared contract, operation count or original recreation acceptance follows from a private study.
